snippet.title: The fascinating reason you loved peek-a-boo
snippet.description:
Dig into how the simple game of peek-a-boo contributes to babies developing their cognitive, motor, and social skills.

--

In Italy, it’s called il gioco del cucù. Palestinians say ba' 'éno. And in Japan, it’s inaīnaibā! Peek-a-boo is a near universal source of laughter and connection for infants and adults— it’s the first game that almost everyone plays. So what is it about this goofy game that babies love so much? Dig into how this simple game promotes the development of our cognitive, motor, and social skills.

snippet.title: Do imaginary friends make you smarter?
snippet.description:
Explore the psychology behind why children invent imaginary companions and what skills they can develop through pretend play.

--

Amia and her friend Zelba have been inseparable for nearly a year. They share secrets, play games, and rule over imaginary kingdoms. Amia sometimes has bad ideas, and Zelba goes along with them anyway. Amia is very real, but Zelba... is not. So, what leads kids to create these fictional figures? Explore why children invent imaginary companions and what skills they can develop through pretend play.

In this video we look at how a national housing boom turns into a bust, why house prices became so unaffordable in the first place, and what it means for an economy when the family home stops being a place to live and becomes a leveraged investment.

Along the way we cover the interest-rate math behind home affordability and why falling mortgage rates inflated prices for forty years, the politics of why governments keep house prices rising, why high housing costs drive young workers to emigrate, and the lessons from past property crashes in Japan, the United States, and Ireland. We also look at Henry George's argument for a land value tax, Edward Leamer's "Housing IS the Business Cycle," and why an efficient property market matters for the whole economy. Whether you're in the US, UK, Canada, Australia, or anywhere else watching house prices climb out of reach, the underlying dynamics are the same.

snippet.title: Did Phil Ivey Cheat? The Casino Scandal That Divided the World
snippet.description:
Phil Ivey is widely regarded as one of the greatest poker players of all time. But in 2012, he found himself at the center of one of the most controversial gambling scandals ever.

Together with Cheung Yin Sun, a gambler known for her extraordinary ability to spot tiny imperfections on playing cards, Ivey won millions from some of the world's most prestigious casinos using a technique called "edge sorting."

Was it genius?
Was it cheating?
Or was it something in between?

In this documentary, we uncover the incredible true story behind the $20 million baccarat scandal that led to courtroom battles in both the United Kingdom and the United States. From the luxury tables of Crockfords Casino in London to the Borgata in Atlantic City, this case changed the gambling industry forever and raised a question that still divides experts today.

 How edge sorting works
 The role of Cheung Yin Sun
Phil Ivey's massive casino wins
 The legal battles that followed
 Why courts ruled against Ivey
 The lasting impact on casinos worldwide

This is the story of a tiny flaw that became worth millions.

snippet.title: The Country That Nobody Cares About
snippet.description:
This isn't an attempt to name and shame one of the least-polluting, poorest nations on the planet for not saving the world single-handedly. It is merely a symbolic reminder of what it means to do our part in a giant system we often feel powerless to control. Saving the world might feel (and perhaps be) impossible, but suffice it to say that if we're going to demand something of others, at the very least we should be doing it ourselves.

snippet.title: The Most Dangerous Man in America: Daniel Ellsberg and the Pentagon Files (Full Documentary)
snippet.description:
In 1971, Daniel Ellsberg, a high-level Pentagon official and Vietnam War strategist, concludes that the war is based on decades of lies and leaks 7,000 pages of top secret documents to The New York Times, hoping to help stop the war he helped plan.

The Most Dangerous Man in America is the riveting story of how one man’s profound change of heart creates a landmark struggle involving America’s newspapers, president and Supreme Court-- a political thriller whose events led directly to Watergate, Nixon’s resignation and the end of the Vietnam War.

-------

Chapters
▷ 00:00 - Introduction

snippet.description: Shan Hanes was the perfect small-town banker. Chairman of the Kansas Bankers Association, known for mowing lawns and coaching sports teams, trusted by everyone in Elkhart. Then in December 2022, someone on WhatsApp convinced him to invest in cryptocurrency. What started with a few thousand became an obsession. He drained his daughter's college fund, stole $40,000 from his church, and finally embezzled $47 million from Heartland Tri-State Bank in just eight weeks. The "pig butchering" crypto scam destroyed a century-old bank and devastated a town of 2,000 people. He got 24 years in prison—Kansas's longest white-collar sentence ever. The FBI recovered $8 million for victims. This is the shocking true story of how trust and desperation collide.

snippet.title: Hedge Fund Collapses: Long-Term Capital Management (LTCM) vs Archegos Capital
snippet.description:
This video dives deep into two of the most shocking financial disasters in modern history: Long-Term Capital Management (LTCM) in the 1990s and Archegos Capital in 2021. Both cases show how brilliant minds, complex mathematical models, and hidden leverage nearly destroyed the global financial system. Through their stories, you’ll learn why concentrated risk and opaque structures remain ticking time bombs in modern markets.

From the so-called 'genius' quants behind LTCM who believed math could conquer risk, to Bill Hwang’s invisible empire at Archegos built on derivatives and total return swaps, we explore how greed, confidence, and technology keep repeating the same mistakes. These tales aren’t just about big money—they’re about human nature, ambition, and the illusion of control.

Across six chapters, we reveal how the Federal Reserve’s secret rescue of LTCM set a precedent for future bailouts and how Archegos exposed the same flaws decades later. This documentary blends storytelling with economic insight, uncovering how fragile our financial architecture truly is in an age of hidden leverage and lightning-fast trading.

If you’ve ever wondered how one single fund can shake the global economy or what hidden risks might still lurk behind today’s hedge funds, this video will keep you on the edge. Understanding these cases means understanding the financial world we all depend on—and the dangers that remain unseen beneath the surface.

snippet.title: Evergrande Liquidation Explained: Inside China's $300 Billion Real Estate Crisis
snippet.description:
The Evergrande crisis revealed the dark side of China’s economic miracle. This video unpacks how one of the world’s largest property developers accumulated over $300 billion in debt, used pre-sales to finance endless expansion, and ultimately sparked fears of a systemic collapse in China’s housing and banking sectors.

We’ll explain how Evergrande’s business model worked—and why it failed. From massive pre-sale schemes that turned homebuyers into unwilling financiers, to debt pyramids that reached every corner of China’s financial system, this story exposes the true fragility behind decades of growth built on borrowed money.

More than just numbers, this is a human story about families who lost savings, workers left unpaid, and a government scrambling to contain chaos. We’ll explore Beijing’s unprecedented efforts to stop the contagion and what this crisis teaches us about trust, capitalism, and financial responsibility in the modern world.

If you’ve ever wondered what happens when optimism meets over-leverage, or how far a nation will go to maintain stability, you’ll want to see this entire breakdown of Evergrande—the giant that built cities and nearly brought China to its knees.

snippet.title: Strike on Iran: The Nuclear Question (updated documentary) | FRONTLINE (PBS)
snippet.description:
An investigation into the status of Iran’s nuclear program amid the second round of U.S.-Israeli military action in less than a year. (March 2026 update)

This journalism is made possible by viewers like you. Donate to FRONTLINE now: https://bit.ly/47DFzCb

And support your local PBS station here: https://www.pbs.org/donate

In the weeks since the U.S. and Israel began bombarding Iran, President Trump has repeatedly justified the strikes by claiming Iran had posed an imminent nuclear threat. But nine months earlier, in the wake of U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran in June 2025, the message coming from Washington was that Iran’s key nuclear facilities had been “obliterated.”

Drawing on new reporting, satellite imagery analysis and interviews, this investigation is an updated presentation of our December 2025 documentary by the same name.

In September of last year, directors Adam Desiderio and Sebastian Walker, who is also the film’s correspondent, visited sites hit in the June 2025 U.S.-Israeli strikes and sat down with one of Iran’s most powerful officials, Ali Larijani — in what turned out to be the last on-camera interview he gave to an American news outlet before his assassination earlier this month in an Israeli airstrike. 

Since the current war began, the team has been talking to experts and officials and analyzing satellite imagery with The Washington Post, Bellingcat and Evident Media to try to understand the truth about what remains of Iran’s nuclear program.

Their findings offer valuable insights into a continuing conflict that has rippled across the Middle East, killing thousands — including children at an elementary school — and displacing millions.

It is written, produced and directed by Adam Desiderio and Sebastian Walker. The correspondent is Sebastian Walker. The reporters are Nilo Tabrizy, Jarrett Ley, Souad Mekhennet, Trevor Ball, Carlos Gonzales and Sebastian Vandermeersch. The senior producers are Dan Edge and Eamonn Matthews. snippet.title: Data Brokers: The Dark Industry of Selling Your Identity for Profit.
snippet.description:
Data Brokers… a dark industry based on selling your identity for profit that is currently worth billions. 

When people say “data is the new oil” there’s no other industry that better illustrates this than the world of data brokers. 

In this video we’ll take a look at exactly how data brokers are taking your personal information and selling it off for a hefty profit… all behind your back.


******

***
𝗟𝗘𝗧'𝗦 𝗖𝗢𝗡𝗡𝗘𝗖𝗧:
📸 IG: james.v.j // https://bit.ly/2TOaBBC
🐦 Twitter: @jamesvjani // https://bit.ly/2zYPrsT

******

YOUR DATA 
Your name, your age, your height, your weight, where you live, where you work, your family, your friends, your likes, your dislikes, your phone number, your email, your health conditions, your buying habits, your credit score, your political beliefs, your religious beliefs, who you text… 

These are all examples of ‘data points’. And these pieces of data are very valuable things.

WHERE IS PERSONAL DATA SOURCED?
In order to source this information, begin by scraping data from public records. Things like: social media pages, property records, court records, birth certificates, voter registration information, bankruptcy records. 

Then go ahead and purchase data from OTHER companies. That’s right: other companies that have your data can make an extra stream of revenue for themselves by selling the information they have on their customers. 

Create “free” websites and services, that collect data from your users. Put ‘trackers’ on these websites/services that detect a user’s location, their contact list, their photos, etc. 

CREATING PROFILES FROM OUR DATA
Finally, once we’ve gathered all this data, we can begin to create ‘profiles’ of individuals. This can detail an individual’s behaviour/personality when it comes to their buying habits, their likes/dislikes, their political affiliations, their health concerns, etc. 

Once we have created these profiles… it’s time to sell! 

SELLING THE DATA
You can sell this information to… pretty much whoever wants it. 

The most common customers that data brokers have at the moment are marketing companies. If a gym had a list of individuals who were interested in getting fit, that would be a very valuable audience for them to target with their advertisements. 

But you can also sell this data to health insurance companies, banks, ‘people search’ websites, governments, and other data brokers. 

THE DILEMMA
Although it sounds quite sinister, this industry does pose a dilemma: if a many of the free websites and apps that you use require your data in order to stay profitable – is it really such a problem? If it’s just being used for marketing purposes, is there a big consequence to that? 

This is a current argument that is going on in the industry at the moment, and it’s one that I have struggled with getting to grips with as well. One thing that I do believe strongly is that the way in which your data is managed should be regulated fare more than it currently is.

snippet.title: Cyber Criminals vs Bangladesh's Central Bank | The $1 Billion Heist
snippet.description:
In February 2016, hackers attempted one of the most audacious bank robberies in history.

After secretly infiltrating the Bangladesh Bank's systems for nearly a year, the attackers used the global SWIFT banking network to initiate fraudulent transfers worth almost $1 BILLION. Their plan was meticulous, their timing was perfect, and for a brief moment, it looked like they might succeed.

But a small mistake changed everything.

This documentary explores the incredible true story of the Bangladesh Bank Heist, the investigation that followed, and the alleged involvement of the notorious Lazarus Group. From hidden malware and international money laundering to casinos in the Philippines and a billion-dollar cybercrime operation, this is one of the most fascinating financial crimes ever uncovered.

How did the hackers get inside the bank?
 Why was nearly $951 million targeted?
 How was most of the money stopped?
 What role did the SWIFT network play?
 Who was behind the attack?

Watch until the end to discover how a single typo may have prevented one of the largest thefts in modern history.

snippet.title: The Art of Irish Beekeeping: The Keepers | Honey Bee Documentary
snippet.description:
Set against the wild beauty of Ireland’s Beara Peninsula, this intimate documentary follows the De Ruiter family and their deep relationship with the honey bee after 25 years of life and beekeeping in Ireland. From pollen to pot, the film offers a poetic and immersive portrait of the apiary process, revealing how honey is shaped by landscape, season, family knowledge and the fragile rhythms of nature.

Through the family’s daily stewardship, the documentary explores the cultural folklore of bees, the urgent environmental challenges facing pollinators today, and the powerful role conscious human care can play in protecting the natural world. Interwoven with original music and poetry, the film journeys alongside the honey bee and its keepers, uncovering a story of resilience, adaptation, ecology and interdependence.

Both lyrical and grounded, this documentary is a moving celebration of Irish beekeeping, sustainable living, family tradition and the quiet intelligence of the honey bee.

snippet.title: ZZZZ Best The $100 Million Teen Fraud That Fooled Wall Street
snippet.description:
This video explores the unbelievable true story of Barry Minkow and his company ZZZZ Best — one of the most shocking financial frauds in American history. At just sixteen, Minkow created a carpet-cleaning business that looked too good to be true, and it was. By the time he was twenty-one, it turned into a $100 million corporate illusion that fooled investors, banks, and even Wall Street.

Across six chapters, we uncover how a teenager built an empire out of lies, why auditors and journalists failed to see the truth, and what his downfall revealed about the culture of greed and blind trust in the 1980s. ZZZZ Best wasn’t just a scam — it was a mirror reflecting society’s obsession with success, fame, and image.

You’ll dive into the rise and fall of Barry Minkow, the charisma that sold a fantasy, and the lessons that still matter today. From fake restoration jobs to a stock market debut built entirely on deception, this story proves how dangerous unchecked ambition can be. It’s a masterclass in fraud, finance, and human psychology — all wrapped in one unbelievable true crime story.

Watch until the end to discover what the $100 million lie of ZZZZ Best can still teach us about modern business, investment, and trust in a world that often prefers image over truth.

Yesterday SpaceX became the largest company ever to go public, in an IPO that values Elon Musk's rocket-and-AI conglomerate at $1.78 trillion. But SpaceX is just the first. Anthropic and OpenAI have both filed to go public, Alphabet has just raised a record $85 billion in new stock, and Meta is reportedly considering doing the same. Goldman Sachs expects as much as $675 billion of new equity to hit the market this year.

For two decades the stock market did nothing but shrink — companies stayed private, bought back their own shares, and got taken private by private equity, leaving less and less stock to go around. That era is now over.
